title: Slow Cooker Carnitas-Style Pork with Orange, Lime and Cumin
description: Pork shoulder braises with citrus and spices until it falls apart, then crisps in a hot skillet so every taco gets tender and crunchy bits. Three pounds feeds eight, about $2 a serving with tortillas.
notes: Look for a shoulder with good marbling; the fat keeps the meat moist and is what crisps in the skillet. Pork is safe at 145°F with a 3-minute rest, but shoulder needs the full cook to pass 195°F and turn tender enough to shred. Thaw the pork in the refrigerator first: never start frozen meat in a slow cooker, and never cook on WARM, which only holds food that is already cooked. Save the strained cooking liquid; a few spoonfuls keep leftovers juicy and it makes a good base for beans or rice. Shredded pork keeps 4 days in the refrigerator and 3 months in the freezer with some of its liquid. Refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat to 165°F, crisping it again in a hot skillet for the best texture.

ingredients.name: boneless pork shoulder, trimmed of thick fat and cut into 3-inch chunks
yellow onion, cut into thick wedges
tomato salsa or pico de gallo

instructions: Pat the pork chunks dry. Stir the salt, cumin, oregano, chili powder and pepper together in a small bowl and rub the mixture all over the pork.
Scatter the onion, garlic and bay leaves over the bottom of a 6-quart slow cooker. Set the pork on top in an even layer and pour the orange juice and lime juice over it.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8 to 10 hours or on HIGH for 5 to 6 hours, until the pork pulls apart with no resistance when pressed with a fork.

Lift the pork onto a rimmed board or tray and discard the bay leaves. Shred it with 2 forks, removing any soft pieces of fat. Strain the cooking liquid into a bowl, let it settle for a few minutes, and spoon off most of the fat that rises.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add half the pork in an even layer and drizzle with 3 tbsp of the cooking liquid. Cook without stirring for 4 to 5 minutes, until the bottom is browned and crisp, then flip in sections and cook 2 minutes more. Repeat with the rest of the pork.
Taste and add salt if needed. Serve the pork in warm corn tortillas with salsa and cilantro, keeping extra cooking liquid on hand to moisten the meat.

title: Slow Cooker Chicken Tortilla Soup with Black Beans and Corn
description: A brothy, gently smoky Mexican-style soup with shredded chicken thighs, black beans and corn, topped with skillet-crisped tortilla strips. Two pounds of chicken make eight big bowls.
notes: The soup should taste bright and a little smoky; if it seems flat, add more lime juice before more salt. Thaw the chicken in the refrigerator first: never start frozen meat in a slow cooker, and always cook on LOW or HIGH, because the WARM setting only holds food that is already cooked. Boneless chicken breasts work in place of the thighs, but check them after 4 hours on LOW, since they dry out sooner. Store the soup and tortilla strips separately so the strips stay crisp; the soup keeps 4 days in the refrigerator and 3 months in the freezer. Refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat to 165°F, about 8 minutes on the stove over medium heat. Check that the corn tortillas are labeled gluten-free if you are cooking for someone with celiac disease.

ingredients.name: fire-roasted diced tomatoes (15 oz), with their juices
black beans (15 oz), drained and rinsed
corn tortillas (6-inch), cut into thin strips

instructions: Put the onion, bell pepper, jalapeño, garlic, tomatoes with their juices, black beans, chili powder, cumin, oregano and 1 tsp of the salt in a 6-quart slow cooker and stir.
Nestle the chicken thighs into the vegetables in a single layer and pour in the broth so the chicken is submerged.

Cover and cook on LOW for 6 hours or on HIGH for 3 hours, until the chicken shreds easily and an instant-read thermometer in the thickest piece reads at least 165°F. Avoid lifting the lid early; each peek adds about 15 minutes.
Lift the chicken onto a cutting board, shred it with 2 forks, and return it to the pot with the frozen corn. Cover and cook on HIGH for 15 minutes, until the corn is hot.

While the corn heats, warm the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Fry the tortilla strips in 2 batches, stirring often, for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden and crisp. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate and sprinkle with the remaining 1/2 tsp salt.
Stir the lime juice into the soup, then taste and adjust the salt. Ladle into bowls and top with the tortilla strips, cilantro and avocado.

title: Slow Cooker Dal Makhani-Style Brown Lentils and Kidney Beans
description: A creamy, buttery Punjabi-style dal made with easy-to-find brown lentils and canned kidney beans in place of whole urad. It simmers all day and costs about $1.25 a bowl with rice.
notes: Brown lentils hold their shape over a long cook better than red lentils, which gives this dal the body of the traditional version. Use canned kidney beans here: dried kidney beans must be boiled hard for 10 minutes before they go into a slow cooker, because the slow cooker alone does not get hot enough to make them safe. For a dairy-free dal, cook the onions in coconut oil and stir in full-fat coconut milk instead of the butter and cream; this removes the milk allergen. The dal thickens a lot as it cools, so thin leftovers with water as you reheat. It keeps 5 days in the refrigerator or 3 months in the freezer. Refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat to 165°F, about 6 minutes on the stove over medium heat, stirring often.

ingredients.name: brown or green lentils (290 g), rinsed and picked over
kidney beans (15 oz), drained and rinsed
serrano or green chile, slit lengthwise

instructions: Melt 2 tbsp of the butter in a 10-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring now and then, for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft and golden at the edges.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric, paprika and cayenne and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant. Add the tomato paste and cook 1 minute more, stirring, until it darkens slightly.
Scrape the onion mixture into a 6-quart slow cooker. Add the lentils, kidney beans, tomato sauce, chile, salt and water and stir well.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8 hours or on HIGH for 5 hours, until the lentils are completely soft and some have broken down into the liquid.

Mash about a quarter of the dal against the side of the pot with a sturdy spoon to make it creamy. Stir in the cream, the remaining 2 tbsp butter and the garam masala, cover, and cook on HIGH for 20 minutes more.
About 30 minutes before serving, rinse the rice until the water runs nearly clear and cook it in a medium saucepan according to the package directions, then let it rest covered for 10 minutes.

Remove the chile, taste the dal and add salt if needed; it should be thick enough to mound softly on a spoon, so stir in hot water a few tablespoons at a time if it is too stiff. Serve over the rice with cilantro.

title: Italian-Style Slow Cooker Sausage, Potato and White Bean Soup with Spinach
description: One pound of Italian sausage seasons a whole pot of potatoes, cannellini beans and tomatoes, enough for eight bowls at roughly $1.75 each. Spinach goes in at the end so it stays green.
notes: Browning the sausage first matters: it builds flavor, lets you leave the extra fat behind, and gets the ground meat to 160°F before the long cook. Never put frozen sausage in a slow cooker, and never cook on WARM, which is meant only for holding food that is already cooked. Kale works in place of spinach; add it 30 minutes before serving so it has time to soften. Some sausages contain wheat fillers, so read the label if you need the soup gluten-free, and leave off the Parmesan for a dairy-free bowl (this removes the milk allergen). The soup keeps 4 days in the refrigerator and 3 months in the freezer, though the potatoes soften a little after freezing. Refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat to 165°F, about 8 minutes on the stove over medium heat.

ingredients.name: fresh sweet or hot italian pork sausage, casings removed
yukon gold potatoes, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
cannellini beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed
parmesan cheese (45 g), finely grated, for serving

instructions: Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the sausage and cook, breaking it into small pieces with a spoon, for 6 to 8 minutes, until browned with no pink left and an instant-read thermometer reads 160°F.

Lift the sausage into a 6-quart slow cooker with a slotted spoon, leaving the fat in the skillet. Lower the heat to medium, add the onion, carrots and celery, and cook for 5 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until the onion softens. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Scrape the vegetables into the slow cooker. Add the potatoes, beans, crushed tomatoes, broth, oregano, red pepper flakes, bay leaf, salt and a few grinds of pepper and stir.
Cover and cook on LOW for 7 hours or on HIGH for 4 hours, until a potato cube crushes easily against the side of the pot.
Remove the bay leaf. Mash a few potato cubes and beans against the side of the pot to thicken the broth slightly, then stir in the spinach a handful at a time; it wilts in about 2 minutes.
Taste and adjust the salt and pepper. Ladle into deep bowls and top with Parmesan.

title: Slow Cooker Chickpea and Spinach Coconut Curry
description: Canned chickpeas simmer in a gingery onion-tomato masala, then get coconut milk and a big handful of spinach at the end. Served over basmati rice, it comes to about $1.50 a bowl.
notes: Cooking the onion and spices in a skillet first takes 10 minutes but gives the curry a much deeper flavor than putting everything in raw. Add the coconut milk at the end, since hours of simmering can make it separate and turn grainy. Kale works in place of spinach; give it 20 minutes on HIGH instead of 5. For a richer, non-vegan version, stir in 1/2 cup plain whole-milk yogurt off the heat at the end (this adds the milk allergen). The curry keeps 5 days in the refrigerator and 3 months in the freezer; freeze it without the rice. Refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat to 165°F, about 6 minutes on the stove over medium heat.

ingredients.name: chickpeas (15 oz each), drained and rinsed
full-fat coconut milk (13.5 oz), shaken well

instructions: Melt the coconut oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring now and then, for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft and golden at the edges.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, chile, cumin, coriander, turmeric and cayenne and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant. Add the tomato paste and cook 1 minute more, stirring, until it darkens slightly.
Scrape the onion mixture into a 6-quart slow cooker. Add the chickpeas, crushed tomatoes, broth and salt and stir well.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6 hours or on HIGH for 3 hours, until the sauce has thickened and the chickpeas are soft enough to crush easily against the side of the pot.
About 30 minutes before serving, rinse the rice until the water runs nearly clear and cook it in a medium saucepan according to the package directions, then let it rest covered for 10 minutes.

Lightly mash about a cup of the chickpeas against the side of the pot to thicken the sauce. Stir in the coconut milk and garam masala, then the spinach a handful at a time. Cover and cook on HIGH for 5 to 10 minutes, until the spinach wilts and the curry is steaming hot.
Stir in the lemon juice, taste, and add salt if needed. Serve over the rice with cilantro.

title: Slow Cooker Southern-Style Barbecue Pulled Chicken with Vinegar Slaw
description: Chicken thighs cook in a tangy tomato-and-vinegar barbecue sauce until they shred, then pile onto buns with a crisp, no-mayo cabbage slaw. Three pounds of thighs feed eight for about $2 a sandwich.
notes: Thighs stay juicy over a long cook; breasts also work, but check them after 3 hours on LOW, since they dry out sooner. Use thawed chicken only: never start frozen meat in a slow cooker, and never cook on WARM, which is meant only for holding cooked food. Many burger buns contain milk or eggs, so read the label if you need this dairy-free or egg-free; for gluten-free, serve the chicken over rice or baked potatoes instead (this removes the wheat allergen). The pulled chicken keeps 4 days in the refrigerator and freezes in its sauce for 3 months, while the slaw is best within 2 days. Refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat to 165°F, covered, over medium-low heat with a splash of water.

ingredients.name: apple cider vinegar, for the sauce
small head green cabbage, cored and thinly sliced (about 6 cups)
apple cider vinegar, for the slaw

instructions: Whisk the ketchup, 1/3 cup vinegar, brown sugar, tomato paste, smoked paprika, chili powder, garlic powder, mustard powder, 1 tsp of the salt, the pepper and the hot sauce together in the bottom of a 6-quart slow cooker.
Scatter the onion over the sauce, then add the chicken thighs and turn them to coat. Arrange them in an even layer.
Cover and cook on LOW for 5 hours or on HIGH for 3 hours, until the chicken pulls apart easily and an instant-read thermometer in the thickest piece reads at least 165°F.

About 30 minutes before the chicken is done, make the slaw: toss the cabbage and carrots in a large bowl with the 3 tbsp vinegar, granulated sugar, olive oil and remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Let it stand, tossing once or twice, until slightly softened.
Shred the chicken right in the slow cooker with 2 forks and stir it into the sauce. If the sauce looks thin, cook uncovered on HIGH for 20 to 30 minutes, until it clings to the meat.
Pile the chicken onto the toasted buns, top with a heap of slaw, and serve the rest of the slaw on the side.

title: Slow Cooker Harira-Inspired Lentil and Chickpea Soup
description: A Moroccan-style tomato soup with lentils, chickpeas, warm spices and plenty of fresh herbs, finished with lemon and a little rice. Vegan, filling, and about $1.25 a bowl.
notes: Harira is often made with lamb and thickened with a flour slurry; this version stays vegan and gluten-free and relies on lentils and rice for body. For broken vermicelli instead of rice, stir in 1/3 cup for the last 20 minutes (this adds wheat). The rice keeps absorbing broth, so leftovers thicken overnight; loosen them with water as you reheat. If you are cooking ahead, freeze the soup before adding the rice for the best texture; it keeps 5 days in the refrigerator and 3 months in the freezer. Refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat to 165°F, about 8 minutes on the stove over medium heat.

ingredients.name: brown or green lentils (190 g), rinsed and picked over

instructions: Put the lentils, chickpeas, crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, onion, celery, carrot, garlic, ginger, turmeric, cumin, paprika, cinnamon, pepper and olive oil in a 6-quart slow cooker. Add half of the cilantro and half of the parsley.
Pour in the broth and water and stir until the tomato paste dissolves. Cover and cook on LOW for 7 hours or on HIGH for 4 hours, until the lentils are tender and the vegetables are soft.
Stir in the rice and salt. Cover and cook on HIGH for 30 to 45 minutes, until the rice is tender all the way through.

Stir in the lemon juice and the rest of the cilantro and parsley. Taste and add more salt or lemon as needed; the soup should be thick but still pour from a ladle, so add a little hot water if it is too dense.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot. Dates and bread on the side are a traditional way to round out the meal.

title: Slow Cooker Honey Garlic Chicken Thighs with Broccoli and Rice
description: Chinese-American takeout flavors at home: chicken thighs cook in honey, soy sauce, garlic and ginger, and the sauce thickens at the end around the broccoli. About $2.25 a plate with rice.
notes: Cut the honey to 1/3 cup if you prefer a less sweet sauce; the cornstarch will still thicken it. Gluten-free tamari can replace the soy sauce to remove the wheat allergen, though it still contains soy. Start with thawed chicken only: frozen meat stays too long in the temperature danger zone in a slow cooker, and the WARM setting is for holding cooked food, not cooking it. Frozen broccoli florets work too; add them straight from the freezer and give them 5 extra minutes. Leftovers keep 4 days in the refrigerator, and the chicken and sauce freeze without the rice for 3 months. Refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat to 165°F, covered, in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes per serving, stirring halfway.
instructions: Whisk the honey, soy sauce, ketchup, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, red pepper flakes and black pepper together in a 6-quart slow cooker until the honey dissolves.

Add the chicken thighs and turn them to coat, then arrange them in a single, slightly overlapping layer. Cover and cook on LOW for 4 to 4 1/2 hours or on HIGH for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, until the chicken is tender and an instant-read thermometer in the thickest piece reads at least 165°F.

About 30 minutes before the chicken is done, rinse the rice and put it in a medium saucepan with 2 1/2 cups of water and the salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 15 minutes, then let it rest off the heat for 10 minutes.

Lift the chicken onto a cutting board. Stir the cornstarch and cold water together in a small bowl until smooth, whisk it into the sauce, and lay the broccoli on top. Cover and cook on HIGH for 15 to 20 minutes, until the sauce is glossy and thick and the broccoli is bright green and crisp-tender.
Meanwhile, cut the chicken into bite-size pieces or shred it with 2 forks. Return it to the slow cooker and fold it gently into the sauce and broccoli.
Spoon the chicken, broccoli and sauce over the rice and scatter with scallions.

title: Slow Cooker Hungarian-Style Beef Goulash with Potatoes and Paprika
description: Beef chuck, a pile of onions and plenty of paprika cook down into a deep red stew with potatoes and carrots. Two and a half pounds of chuck feed eight, at about $3 a bowl.
notes: Beef chuck is safe once it passes 145°F with a 3-minute rest, but it needs the long cook to reach about 200°F, where its connective tissue melts and the meat turns tender. Thaw the beef in the refrigerator first: never put frozen meat in a slow cooker, and never cook on WARM, which only holds food that is already cooked. Use fresh, bright red paprika; old paprika tastes dusty and makes a dull stew. A spoonful of sour cream on each bowl is common in many homes (it adds the milk allergen), and caraway can be left out if you do not have it. Goulash keeps 4 days in the refrigerator and 3 months in the freezer, though the potatoes soften a little after freezing. Refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat to 165°F, about 10 minutes on the stove over medium heat.

ingredients.name: boneless beef chuck roast, trimmed and cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
yellow onions, halved and thinly sliced
paprika (sweet Hungarian if you have it)
yukon gold potatoes, cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks
carrots, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
red bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces
chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley, for serving

instructions: Put the potatoes, carrots and bell pepper in the bottom of a 6-quart slow cooker; the root vegetables cook slowest, so they go closest to the heat.

Pat the beef dry and season it with 1 tsp of the salt and the pepper. Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat and brown half the beef on 2 sides, about 6 minutes, without crowding. Lay it over the vegetables and repeat with the remaining oil and beef.
Lower the heat to medium and add the onions to the skillet. Cook, stirring and scraping up the browned bits, for 10 to 12 minutes, until soft and light golden.

Take the skillet off the heat and stir in the garlic, paprika and caraway for 30 seconds; paprika scorches and turns bitter over direct heat. Stir in the tomato paste and 1 cup of the broth, scraping the pan clean.

Pour the onion mixture over the beef, then add the remaining 1 cup broth, the bay leaf and the remaining 1 tsp salt. Do not worry that the liquid does not cover everything; the beef and vegetables release their own juices.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8 hours or on HIGH for 5 to 6 hours, until the beef is fork-tender and a potato chunk breaks apart when pressed.
Remove the bay leaf, skim the fat from the surface with a wide spoon, and stir gently. Taste for salt and serve in bowls with parsley.

title: Slow Cooker Black-Eyed Pea and Collard Green Stew with Smoked Paprika
description: Dried black-eyed peas need no soaking: they cook all day with vegetables and smoked paprika, then collards and tomatoes go in for the last hour. One pound of peas makes eight bowls at about $1 each.
notes: Black-eyed peas cook through without soaking and are safe to start dry in a slow cooker; that is not true of dried kidney beans, which must be boiled hard for 10 minutes first. The tomatoes and vinegar wait until the end because acid can stop peas from softening. If the peas are still firm after the full time, old peas are usually the cause; keep cooking on HIGH and check every 30 minutes. Lacinato or curly kale can replace the collards and needs only 30 minutes. The stew keeps 5 days in the refrigerator and 3 months in the freezer, and it thickens as it sits, so add a splash of water when reheating. Refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat to 165°F, about 8 minutes on the stove over medium heat.

ingredients.name: dried black-eyed peas (454 g), picked over and rinsed
collard greens (about 1 lb), stems removed, leaves cut into 1-inch ribbons
fire-roasted diced tomatoes (15 oz), with their juices
louisiana-style cayenne pepper hot sauce, for serving

instructions: Put the black-eyed peas, olive oil, onion, bell pepper, celery, carrots, garlic, smoked paprika, thyme, red pepper flakes and bay leaves in a 6-quart slow cooker.

Pour in the broth and water and stir; the liquid should cover the peas by about 2 inches. Cover and cook on LOW for 7 hours or on HIGH for 4 hours, until the peas are tender but still holding their shape.

While the peas cook, wash the collard leaves well in a sink of cold water, lifting them out so the grit stays behind. Strip the leaves from the stems, stack them, roll them up and slice into 1-inch ribbons.

Stir the collards, tomatoes with their juices, salt and several grinds of pepper into the stew, pressing the greens under the liquid. Cover and cook on HIGH for 1 hour, until the collards are silky and tender.
Remove the bay leaves. Mash a ladleful of peas against the side of the pot to thicken the broth slightly, then stir in the vinegar.
Taste and add salt if needed. Ladle into bowls and pass hot sauce at the table.
